Source v142.19 still has `html,body{height:100%}` and the `body` declaration `min-height:100vh;min-height:100dvh;min-height:-webkit-fill-available`, as well as `display:flex`, `overflow:hidden`, bottom padding. R20's minimal patch removed the problematic `html{height:-webkit-fill-available}` rule but **did not** replace the entire viewport/safe-area flex-sizing architecture. Residual iOS WebKit height calculations are **a plausible testable hypothesis, not a demonstrated cause of these screenshots**.
2. `#main-content{display:flex;flex:1 1 auto;min-height:0;overflow:hidden}`, `.screen.active{display:flex}`, `#reader-scroll` inherits `.scroll{flex:1;min-height:0;overflow-y:auto}`, and `#nav{position:fixed;bottom:0}`. This architecture can allow visible bottom navigation while the Reader flex chain is wrongly sized or scrolled, so visible nav does **not** prove Reader geometry correct.
3. Short Reader mode is driven by `readerMinimumUsefulHeightPx`, `readerLowHeightDecision`, `updateReaderLowHeightMode`; the compact mode hides global nav when activated. The supplied landscape screenshot shows global nav **visible**, suggesting compact mode was either not activated or the user was on an older build; neither follows uniquely from pixels.
4. `scheduleSemanticLayoutRestore` listens to `resize`, `orientationchange` and `visualViewport.resize`, delays ~180 ms, then invokes `updateReaderLowHeightMode`, root-scroll resets and semantic reading-position restoration in nested animation frames. Actual iOS visual-viewport transitions or stale semantic anchors could influence the symptom; an instrumented iOS trace is required to distinguish these from root CSS sizing.
5. `renderHighlights` in *Mon Espace* calls `openUserRecordTarget`, which uses `goToEntry`/`openEntry` and a `pendingParaId` when opening an ordinary selected highlight. The target restoration path must be tested separately from ordinary entry opening. A `#reader-scroll`/screen flex-height error, late reflow, or misplaced position restoration are competing hypotheses. Avoid edits to IndexedDB/highlight schemas to address a purely visible issue.
6. Source renders the public version pill on **Accueil** as `v` + `PUBLIC_VERSION`. This is the safest low-effort verification. App screenshot hostname `louisriv26.github.io` alone does not distinguish the Beta and production paths on the same GitHub Pages origin.

It was not dishonest evidence, but **it never closed the physical gate**. A minimum one-line CSS guess is unsafe without confirming the real served version and measuring all ancestors, viewport properties, target scroll position and timing.

## B. R19 new actual live-hosted finding — **WebKit inner Reader scrolling FAIL; Chromium contrast PASS**

- Linux WebKit mobile 390×844: document/body **1832px**; `#reader-scroll` **1562px** tall, bottom **1686px**, scrollHeight ≈ clientHeight (no independent Reader scrolling), root scroll max **988px**. At 844×390: body **1339px**, Reader scroll **1080px**, bottom **1204px**, root scroll max **949px**. At 1024×768 iPad-like: body **1339px**, Reader **1080px**, root scroll max **571px**. WebKit nonmobile context gives same failure pattern. Reader text is visible and ordinary Tome entry `LDC.T01.SEC003.P005` was actually opened; this is **not** an editorial-routing false negative.
- Chrome mobile 390×844: body **844px**, Reader **570px**, inner scrollHeight **1568px** (scroll works), no root overflow. Chrome 844×390: body **390px**, Reader **130px** tall, inner scrollHeight **1084px**. Chrome 1024×768: body **768px**, Reader **508px** tall. Chrome nonmobile corroborates. Navigation `#nav` remained bottom-fixed in baseline contexts; separate owner report of half-screen Mon Espace gap remains unadjudicated.
- **New controlled counterfactual:** ephemeral `html{height:100% !important}` on unmodified real-hosted WebKit immediately restores correct viewport body and Reader scrolling in portrait/landscape/iPad-like sizes; Chrome unaffected. Only `body{min-height:0 !important}` or forcing body `height:100%` does **not** solve; bounding body by `100dvh` or bounding `#main-content` does. Hidden-body short-content control shrinks overflow. WebKit large text remains FAIL untreated. R19 portrait baseline after removing style had ~35px layout drift (recorded, no false perfect-reversibility claim); other sizes restored baseline.
- **Cause classification:** Very strong **source declaration–level** evidence implicates `html{height:-webkit-fill-available}` in a Linux WebKit intrinsic/flex sizing interaction, unlike Chrome. Exact internal sizing chain has plausible alternatives and actual Apple Safari has **not been tested**. Minimal proposed successor remedy is remove/replace only that HTML declaration while retaining existing `height:100%`, followed by serious negative-screen and physical QA. This is **a proposal only**, not an authorised mutation. Full counterfactuals/limitations in `LDC_v142.18_R19_ROOT_CAUSE_PROOF_AND_LIMITATIONS_2026-10-08.md`.

## 1. Why v142.15 exists

Post-freeze adversarial review of v142.14 found two small but real candidate-specific truth/consistency defects worth closing before production:

1. **E-15 — unsupported public qualification wording.** The Sources text said that `Par le sens` was `qualifié séparément`, while its own metadata did not support that public qualification claim. v142.15 replaces this with the narrower and accurate statement that `Par le sens` uses a distinct search engine **not covered by the textual-correction campaign described there**.
2. **E-07 — visible documentary/search-scope contradiction.** With a documentary view selected, the screen could imply that all search obeyed that documentary scope even though `Par le sens` intentionally continues to search the normal-reading corpus. v142.15 adds a conditional disclosure: **`Par le sens recherche toujours dans la lecture normale.`** It does **not** alter retrieval, ranking, filters or the semantic corpus universe.

The broader inherited search findings from the adversarial audit are deliberately **not** mixed into this release. They remain a separate post-release search-integrity programme. In particular, future semantic-pack work must address asset identity/versioning/integrity before rebuilding the semantic index.

## 2. Why v142.14 exists

v142.13 had passed its pre-physical qualification, but a later post-freeze blind audit found two material release-truth defects and two further current-binding/staleness issues during the v142.14 continuation work. These findings reject v142.13 as the final successor candidate without implying corruption of the protected corpus, Search-V2, PLS pack, reader, session, backup or user data.

### Defect A — public validation wording conflated two separate semantic-search lanes

**Root cause:** current public Sources/validation wording inherited language that could make the active **Par le sens** function appear to be the same unfinished lane as legacy **Semantic Search V3**.

**Correction:** v142.14 explicitly separates the active `pls_v15` Par-le-sens user function from the legacy Semantic Search V3 historical/fail-closed subsystem. No new scientific or calibration claim is introduced.

### Defect B — stale migration-concurrency gate truth

**Root cause:** `migration_concurrency_residual` remained marked OPEN even though the Stage-8 startup migration gate, exclusive-lock path, fail-closed behavior and rollback protection were already present in the actual runtime.

**Correction:** metadata now reflects the actual runtime. The migration algorithm itself was not changed. Fresh adversarial migration testing is **7/7 PASS**.

### Defect C — incomplete v142.14 Service Worker rebinding during provisional work

**Root cause:** the first v142.14 SW edit advanced the release identity but left shell/runtime cache namespace strings tied to v142.13.

**Correction:** all current SW release/cache identities are v142.14-specific. Fresh upgrade simulation passes both from v142.10 and from the immediate predecessor v142.13.

### Defect D — pre-freeze status strings would have become stale on packaging

**Root cause:** provisional v142.14 metadata still contained current-looking `IN_PROGRESS`, `PENDING_FINAL_FREEZE` and related qualification wording after the relevant machine work had completed.

**Correction:** current fields now say precisely what has passed and what remains open. Production authorization remains false.

### QA-harness defect — predecessor package manifest misclassified as a fifth app mutation

The inherited static harness counted the intentionally removed v142.13 `PACKAGE_MANIFEST_SHA256.json` as a fifth application mutation. That is a **test-classification defect**, not an application defect. The governing mutation rule is:

1. exactly four application/release replacements relative to v142.13: `index.html`, `version.json`, `offline_manifest.json`, `sw.js`;
2. predecessor package manifest discarded because it describes predecessor bytes;
3. fresh v142.14 qualification evidence generated separately;
4. fresh v142.14 package manifest generated **last**.

## 2. Why v142.12 exists

v142.11 correctly implemented the principal documentary-reading redesign but its post-freeze re-audit found that its release qualification was too optimistic. The defects did **not** show corpus corruption, Search regression, provenance-record corruption or failure of the new paragraph/selection-aware provenance architecture. They were consistency defects:

1. public provenance copy still called all `2 312` technical PRINCIPAL records “entrées PRINCIPAL”, although only `2 296` are user-visible PRINCIPAL reading entries;
2. a stale `||74` complement-count fallback remained;
3. additional hard-coded `75 / 13 / 62` fallbacks duplicated registry truth in documentary UI paths;
4. Help under-described the documentary behavior of Repères and the local provenance behavior of `Infos et source` / sharing;
5. Stage-2 figures could be read too broadly as if every COMPLÉMENT had followed an identical validation pathway;
6. onboarding still taught a PRINCIPAL-only first mental model;
7. several top-level current-release metadata fields still described earlier v139/v141/v142 work.

v142.11 was therefore **not promoted and not accepted as a production candidate**. v142.12 is the bounded closure of those defects.

## 1. Authorized change and implementation result

v142.11 implements the previously approved documentary-reading UX/provenance redesign from the exact production v142.10 bytes. It does not reopen the conceptual decision.

### 1.1 Normal reading contract

Normal reading remains the existing composite of **PRINCIPAL + retained COMPLÉMENTS at their governed positions**. The old internal value `enriched` remains supported for backward compatibility but is no longer presented as the ordinary public reading concept.

The permanent three-way source selector is removed from normal Bibliothèque/Tome/Reader/Search surfaces. A secondary **Vue documentaire** now contains:

- **Lecture normale**;
- **Corpus principal uniquement**;
- **Compléments uniquement**.

A non-normal documentary view is never silent: compact status surfaces remain visible on the ordinary navigation/reading/search screens and provide **Revenir à la lecture normale** plus **Changer**.

### 1.2 Persistent choice vs temporary/navigation override

`setSupplementMode(mode, opts)` now distinguishes origin and persistence. Only an explicit user choice from **Vue documentaire** may write `settings.supplement_mode`. Navigation, temporary Reader target-opening and legacy/deep-link source scope do not silently overwrite that saved preference.

Legacy values remain accepted:

- `enriched` → Lecture normale;
- `aflp` → Vue documentaire · Corpus principal;
- `additions` → Vue documentaire · Compléments;
- historical `supplements` continues to migrate to `additions`.

Old deep-link values `src=principal`, `src=complement`, `src=enrichi` remain supported.

### 1.3 Local documentary provenance resolver

A separate `resolveReaderDocumentaryContext()` layer was added. `activeReaderSupplement()` was not repurposed and remains byte-identical to v142.10.

Resolver priority is implemented as:

1. valid selection bound to the current Reader;
2. explicit paragraph target;
3. valid current context paragraph;
4. top/active visible paragraph;
5. Reader focus;
6. entry-level fallback.

The result distinguishes `principal`, `supplement` and `mixed` and returns exact paragraph IDs and supplement IDs. Mixed selections do not collapse to one provenance.

The resolver/snapshot is routed into:

- **Infos et source**;
- **Partager la référence** and human-readable references;
- **Copier le lien** reference text;
- support/source label;
- **Signaler un problème de texte**;
- **Autour de ce passage** target/query context.

`Infos et source`, report and Autour capture a frozen documentary snapshot so later scrolling/focus cannot silently change the object being described.

### 1.4 Complement presentation and accessibility

Internal complements remain visibly distinguished with **Repères OFF** through the existing documentary block treatment. **Repères ON** additionally exposes the explicit complement/provenance banner. The internal complement container receives an accessible documentary-boundary label while the visual banner is `aria-hidden` to reduce duplicate VoiceOver output. Complete-entry complement identity remains separately visible.

### 1.5 Secondary consistency repairs

The same bounded successor also closes the contractually identified presentation inconsistencies:

- supplement date rows no longer expose `entrée null`; they use `complément interne` or `entrée complémentaire` where appropriate;
- normal-reading read statistics no longer treat an internal complement as a separate read-entry credit/denominator item; complete-entry complements remain legitimate entries;
- public Help/provenance/search labels use **Lecture normale / Vue documentaire / Corpus principal / Compléments** rather than normal-reader `ENRICHI` jargon;
- the public documentary notice still states the unchanged governed counts: 75 complements / 177 paragraphs / 13 complete entries / 62 internal complements / 74,528 Search-V2 textual records in normal-reading index scope.

## 1. Governing decision

v142.10 is a deliberately bounded user-facing successor to the exact frozen v142.9 `Par le sens` implementation. It does **not** change how a query is composed, canonicalized, prepared, embedded, retrieved, fused, ranked, superseded, or opened. It changes only how semantic results and semantic-unavailable states are explained and visually structured for the user, plus the minimum release identity surfaces required by a new frozen version.

The reason for the successor is UX clarity: the v142.9 results screen exposed internal/development terminology (`PROTOTYPE PERSONNEL`, `DENSE + BM25`, `SEARCH-V3`, `ENRICHI` in the results heading) and uncalibrated confidence-style labels (`Proche par le sens`, `Quelques pistes possibles`). Those labels were technically descriptive but not decision-useful to a normal reader and could imply a level of confidence/calibration that the ranking scores do not provide.

The new public contract is intentionally plain-language and scientifically narrower: the application says that passages are **classified/ranked by proximity to the user’s description**, not that the first result is known to be correct.

## 2. Exact v142.10 user-facing contract

For a successful `Par le sens` search, the normal results area now presents:

- heading: **`Recherche par le sens`**;
- explanation: **`Passages classés selon leur proximité avec votre description.`**;
- native disclosure: **`Comment ça marche ?`**;
- disclosure text: **`La recherche compare votre description aux passages du Livre du Ciel et les classe selon leur proximité. Le premier passage n’est pas nécessairement celui que vous recherchez : ouvrez les résultats qui semblent correspondre et vérifiez leur contexte.`**

Semantic result cards now prioritize information in this order:

1. **Tome + date** as the primary metadata line;
2. passage title where available;
3. excerpt;
4. genuine context badges only where applicable (`COMPLÉMENT`, active Jésus filter);
5. stable technical reference as secondary metadata: `Référence : …`.

The following labels are removed from the ordinary semantic-results UI:

- `PROTOTYPE PERSONNEL`;
- `DENSE + BM25`;
- `SEARCH-V3 · qualification en cours`;
- `Recherche par le sens · ENRICHI`;
- `Proche par le sens`;
- `Quelques pistes possibles`.

The internal ranking engine and diagnostic evidence remain available technically; they are simply no longer presented as normal reader-facing result labels.

## 3. Semantic unavailable-state contract

The exceptional unavailable state is also simplified so that the application does not revert to laboratory terminology when something fails.

User-visible behavior:

- heading remains `Recherche par le sens`;
- message: `Recherche par le sens indisponible pour le moment.`;
- the app explicitly states that the user’s description was **not silently replaced** by a `Par les mots` search;
- if Tome/date/reference criteria were recognized, the user receives a plain-language note that those criteria were recognized but `Par le sens` remains unavailable;
- internal technical reason/status is logged for diagnostics rather than exposed in the normal UI.

This preserves the fail-closed semantic-search principle from v142.9.

## 4. Help/offline wording reconciliation

The Help copy was reconciled to the same public terminology:

- `Par le sens` is described as a user function rather than `prototype personnel`;
- the guidance on describing remembered content, rereading/correcting the description, uncertain Tome/date constraints, cold preparation, and Wi‑Fi remains intact;
- results are described as passages ranked by proximity, with an explicit instruction to verify context;
- the offline section continues to state truthfully that `Par le sens` uses separately loaded resources and is not covered by the standard offline preparation.

Technical diagnostics may still identify Dense/BM25/RRF internals because diagnostics are not ordinary user-facing UI.

## 1. Current decision

v142.8 is the bounded successor to frozen v142.7. It closes the confirmed `Par le sens` interaction/correctness defects without changing corpus content or retrieval/ranking algorithms. Machine/adversarial pre-physical QA passes. The exact candidate is now immutable. It may proceed to App-Test, but it is **not** authorized for production until the exact deployed bytes pass physical iPhone/iPad checks and deployment binding is separately confirmed.

## 2. Why v142.8 was required

The independent post-freeze review of v142.7 confirmed:

1. **Stale semantic result ownership defect.** A semantic search captured a generation in `runSearch()`, but downstream semantic completion could validate against the mutable global generation rather than its own launch generation. An obsolete A search could therefore render after a newer B search.
2. **Owner-runtime initialization concurrency weakness.** The protected owner runtime can expose `index` before tokenizer/model initialization is fully complete. v142.8 does not mutate that protected runtime; it adds a single application-level preparation promise so the application treats the whole `init()` promise as the readiness authority.
3. **Search activity was too weakly signalled.** v142.8 gives the submit action a real busy state and a nearby live progress status.
4. **Semantic composition needed a reviewable editor.** `Par le sens` now uses a native bounded auto-growing textarea while `Par les mots` remains the existing native single-line search input.
5. **The old 240-character deep-link limit contradicted validated semantic use.** One protected real semantic query is 301 characters. Semantic query links now use a canonical bounded 1024-character contract.
6. **The published-version validator rejected N.M public subversions.** It now accepts the governed `N` or `N.M` public version forms, including `142.8`.

## 5. v142.8 search interaction contract

### Par les mots

- keeps native `<input type="search">`;
- keeps `enterkeyhint="search"`;
- Enter/Search may submit as before;
- Search-V2 algorithms are unchanged.

### Par le sens

- uses a native `<textarea>`;
- starts at 3 rows;
- auto-grows to a bounded maximum of approximately 8 text lines, then scrolls internally;
- `maxlength=1024` aligns the composition surface with the deep-link canonical bound;
- Enter creates a new line rather than implicitly submitting;
- the explicit `Rechercher` button commits the draft;
- human formatting may contain line breaks, but execution/storage/sharing canonicalizes semantic whitespace to single spaces and trims it.

Guidance intentionally teaches **several relevant remembered clues**, not “write as much as possible.” It also warns against asserting an uncertain Tome/date because recognized structural information may restrict the search.

## 6. Search execution state model

The governing model is:

`DRAFT → PREPARING (cold semantic only) → SEARCHING → RESULTS / ERROR`

Every committed execution owns an immutable generation token. Editing, clearing, changing mode, or committing a newer search supersedes the old generation immediately. Obsolete work may finish computationally because the protected semantic runtime does not expose true inference cancellation, but obsolete work has **no render authority**.

Owner semantic inference is serialized at the app layer. A newer query waits for an already-running obsolete inference to finish, then checks generation ownership before starting. This avoids concurrent model execution and ensures latest-query ownership without pretending to provide physical cancellation.

Visible phases:

- cold semantic: `Préparation de Par le sens…` → `Recherche des passages…`
- warm semantic: `Recherche des passages…`
- structural-only semantic input: `Recherche dans les références…` and **no semantic runtime initialization**
- submit button while active: `Recherche en cours…`

The progress area has `role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`, `aria-atomic="true"`; the form carries `aria-busy` while active. Animated dots are decorative only and reduced-motion leaves the stable text visible.

## 7. Deep-link/update identity closure

- semantic query canonical limit: **1024 characters**;
- multiline whitespace is canonicalized before link generation;
- the 301-character protected real query round-trips successfully;
- 1024 canonical characters are accepted; 1025 are rejected;
- attempting to copy an over-bound query link fails closed with a user message rather than generating an invalid link;
- published update metadata accepts simple public versions `N` or `N.M` and derives `142.8` correctly from the technical identity.

## D. Newly identified findings to challenge adversarially

### D1 — Query composition affordance
Current semantic guidance invites a natural remembered description, but the control remains a single-line `<input type="search">`.

The prototype's three stored real remembered-query instances are approximately 39–58 words / roughly 200–300 characters and achieved ranks 9 / 2 / 1 in the frozen full hybrid.

**Hypothesis to challenge:** a small auto-growing multi-line semantic composition field may better match the way the prototype was actually validated, while `Par les mots` should remain compact.

Questions:
- Is a textarea truly needed, or can a single-line field plus wording remain simpler/better?
- Would changing input type create keyboard, form-submit, accessibility, persistence or deep-link regressions?
- If multi-line is justified, should it be 2–5 lines, or another design?
- Is auto-growth necessary, or does it add complexity without enough benefit?

### D2 — Guidance strength
Existing wording says exact words are unnecessary but does not clearly teach that multiple **relevant remembered clues** may improve discrimination.

Proposed principle:
`Give several relevant clues you genuinely remember; do not worry about exact wording.`

Potential clues include idea, image/comparison, context, what Jesus/Luisa said, and trusted Tome/date/speaker filters.

**Challenge required:** avoid unsupported “the more text, the better” claims. Determine what is justified by the actual Dense+BM25/RRF implementation and stored real-query evidence. Wrong hard filters may exclude the intended passage.

### D3 — Search-in-progress visibility
v142.7 currently uses `#search-meta`, styled at 12px/muted, positioned after filters/date controls. The submit button continues to read `Rechercher`. The message is static:
`PROTOTYPE PERSONNEL · chargement/recherche…`

The user reports that it is still not obvious the search is running.

**Hypothesis to challenge:** a dedicated prominent busy state near the submit action is warranted.

Candidate ideas:
- button changes to `Recherche en cours`;
- CSS-animated three dots or subtle spinner;
- dedicated busy panel immediately below the button;
- result/output region explicitly owned by the active search;
- keyboard dismissal/reveal of the busy state after explicit submission.

Do not assume all of these are needed. Adversarially assess which minimal combination solves the problem.

### D4 — Honest progress phases
The owner runtime exposes `ready`, `loading`, `available`, plus `init()` and `search()`.

**Hypothesis to challenge:** the UI can honestly distinguish:
1. `Préparation de Par le sens` while the protected runtime initializes;
2. `Recherche des passages` during actual query execution.

Potential benefit: clearer first-use explanation and a chance to stop an obsolete query from entering inference after initialization finishes.

Constraints:
- no fake percentages;
- do not mutate `pls_v15/**`;
- do not preload large semantic resources merely on mode selection unless adversarial review proves that is preferable;
- structural-only queries (Tome/date/reference only) should not misleadingly show semantic-model preparation if they route to structured Search-V2.

### D5 — Potential stale-result race (P1 candidate finding)
`runSearch()` captures a generation value from `searchRunSeq`, but `runSemanticSearchV3(raw)` currently does not receive that captured generation. After asynchronous semantic work it checks `isSearchActive(searchRunSeq)` using the **current global value**.

**Potential failure:** Query A begins, the user edits/starts Query B, A later completes, and A may validate against the new global generation rather than its own launch generation.

This finding must be independently reproduced or disproved from the exact v142.7 code. If confirmed, it is a functional-correctness issue, not merely UX.

Candidate repair if confirmed:
- pass the captured generation through `runSemanticSearchV3(raw, generation)`;
- recheck after initialization, before inference, after inference, and immediately before render;
- also bind rendering to the committed query;
- create a permanent regression: A starts → B supersedes → A finishes last → A must never render.

### D6 — Duplicate submission / output ownership
Current button is disabled only when the query is empty. Assess whether repeated Search taps can launch redundant work and whether the result/output area always unambiguously belongs to the newest execution.

Do not overclaim that old results universally remain; query mutation already clears some output. Test exact cases:
- same-query double tap;
- filter rerun;
- mode switch;
- query edit;
- clear;
- A/B asynchronous completion ordering.

### D7 — Accessibility / motion
If animated dots are used:
- do not repeatedly mutate an `aria-live` string on every dot;
- dots should be visual/decorative (`aria-hidden`);
- stable phase text should be announced;
- `aria-busy` should reflect real busy state;
- reduced-motion users must retain an unmistakable non-animated busy state.

### D8 — Cancellation semantics
Do not add an `Annuler` button unless it truthfully stops the expensive operation. Logical supersession of stale results is not equivalent to aborting model/resource loading/inference. Evaluate whether current AbortController reaches semantic runtime; do not promise more than the code does.

## E. Candidate design previously recommended — NOT YET AUTHORIZED

A possible successor was labelled `v142.8 — Par le sens interaction closure`, with tentative scope:

- richer but concise semantic inline guidance;
- possibly multi-line 2–5-line semantic query control;

## 1. Why v142.5 exists

The post-freeze adversarial recheck of v142.4 found one genuine release-blocking defect in the Reader source selector. At a 320 px viewport with `Grand` text, the short `ENRICHI` label required about 70 px of intrinsic content width while the button client width was about 67 px. v142.4 prevented the text from painting over its neighbour by using `overflow:hidden`, so the button could clip the label while the then-current QA still reported PASS.

The QA weakness was causal: the v142.4 selector gate established non-intersection and a limited span-width condition, but it did not require both `scrollWidth <= clientWidth` and complete visible-label bounding-box containment without overflow masking. Therefore “no overlap” was incorrectly treated as equivalent to “fully readable”.

v142.4 is consequently **superseded and not approved for owner device acceptance**. Its frozen bytes remain immutable historical evidence.

## 3. Reader selector closure

At phone widths (`<=420px`):

- the existing short source labels remain authoritative;
- the three source buttons remain a structural three-column grid;
- `overflow:hidden` is removed from the Reader source buttons, so clipping cannot conceal a failed geometry case;
- `Petit` and `Normal` may remain beside the Reader back control where they fit;
- `Grand` and `Très grand` put the source grid on its **own row**;
- the user's requested reader text size is never reduced to make the controls fit.

The stricter selector gate requires, for every button:

1. no intersection with the adjacent button;
2. complete button containment inside the selector segment;
3. complete visible-label bounding-box containment inside its own button;
4. `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`;
5. no `overflow:hidden` masking;
6. explicit own-row placement for `Grand` and `Très grand`.

The current matrix covers seven widths (`320`, `360`, `375`, `390`, `393`, `414`, `420`) × four text levels (`Petit`, `Normal`, `Grand`, `Très grand`) = **28/28 PASS**.

The exact formerly missed `320 px + Grand` case now passes with three source buttons each measuring `clientWidth=102`, `scrollWidth=102`, `overflowX=visible`, and `own_row=true`.

## 3. P0 canonical Reader-selection repair

The root cause was a stale canonical text-node registry after DOM mutations such as highlight wrapping/unwrapping/normalization and transient search-mark removal. Canonical offsets were correct at initial fragment indexing, but later `Range` endpoints could refer to replacement/split text nodes no longer present in the registry. A visually stable iOS selection could therefore fail canonical mapping.

The bounded repair now:

- exposes a same-fragment `reindexCanonicalFragment(...)` operation that retains the authoritative canonical paragraph text and canonical interval while rebuilding only the live text-node map;
- reindexes after persistent `surroundContents(...)` highlight painting;
- reindexes after highlight unwrap + `normalize()`;
- reindexes after legacy highlight painting;
- reindexes after transient search-mark insertion/removal;
- when a canonical endpoint encounters an unregistered ordinary text node, performs **one** same-fragment reindex-and-retry;
- if that retry still cannot establish a safe canonical position, remains **fail-closed**;
- does **not** add nearest-paragraph guessing or cross-fragment heuristic snapping.

Machine/browser tests proved exact canonical offsets for plain selection, selection across an existing highlight, selection after persistent paint, stale-map self-heal after unwrap/normalize, stale-map self-heal after transient removal, two-fragment and three-fragment selection, backward native selection, and fail-closed rejection of an endpoint outside canonical Reader fragments.

## 4. Interaction precedence repair

`onParaClick(...)` now gives a live native text selection priority over a tap landing on an existing `<mark class="hl">`. A just-captured Safari selection also retains precedence for a short bounded interval if Safari collapses the visible selection immediately before dispatching its synthetic click.

Adversarial browser tests confirmed:

- live native selection + click on an existing highlight → **selection action wins**;
- collapsed/no native selection + click on the same highlight → **existing-highlight edit still wins**.

This changes precedence only; highlight data/persistence semantics are unchanged.

## 5. Reader source selector repair

At phone width the Reader source-mode control now uses the already-existing short labels and a structural three-column grid. At `Très grand` text size it can stack the back control and source grid onto separate rows. The repair does **not** reduce the Reader text size requested by the user.

Fresh browser geometry checks passed for **16/16 combinations**:

- widths: `320`, `375`, `390`, `420` px;
- text levels: `Petit`, `Normal`, `Grand`, `Très grand`;
- zero button intersection;
- selected short labels remain within their own source-button geometry.

## 6. Selection-failure wording and Reader toast clearance

The residual wording `Sélection instable…` is removed. The bounded failure message is now:

`Cette sélection n’a pas pu être reconnue. Réessayez.`

When Reader navigation is present, toast placement is calculated above the `.entry-nav` zone and reserves both the toast’s 20 px entrance animation and a 12 px visual gap. The browser challenge verified that the animated toast never crosses the `Entrée précédente / Lu / Entrée suivante` navigation region.

## 7. Search-progress behavior

The semantic retrieval algorithm is unchanged. The user-facing waiting state is now exposed before the awaited semantic search begins. For the owner full-hybrid path the visible state is:

`Recherche par le sens · PROTOTYPE PERSONNEL · chargement/recherche…`

The output region is revealed immediately and two animation frames are allowed before the slow semantic operation is started. A browser test with an intentionally delayed semantic stub observed the progress state visibly **before completion**, proving that a cold first run no longer appears silent while the model/runtime is loading or searching.

1. `index.html` declared `APP_VERSION = v2.19.142.1-R1B-PLS-OWNER-PROTOTYPE`, but `PUBLIC_VERSION` used the integer-only parser `/v2\.19\.(\d+)/`, so the application would identify itself publicly as **142**, not **142.1**.
2. `index.html` retained the production-v142 `SW_CACHE_VERSION = ldc-v2.19.142-R1B-ux-access-r15`, while the v142.1 `sw.js` declared `VERSION = ldc-v2.19.142.1-R1B-pls-owner-prototype`. `version.json` and `offline_manifest.json` also retained the old v142 `page_worker_revision`. The service worker explicitly checks these identities during installation, so the v142.1 shell install was fail-closed and could not be considered deployable.

The re-audit also found a non-runtime evidence inconsistency: the v142.1 machine-QA `added_files` ledger did not describe the final packaged file set exactly. This did not alter retrieval output but confirmed that the original QA was not sufficiently self-auditing.

Therefore:

## 1. Decision and release position

The v141 single-scroll/adaptive-reveal repair was physically successful on iPhone for the original Search result-readability/scrolling defect. A new physical defect was then discovered on the same exact v141 candidate: after manually entering a query such as `Professeur`, the application could display `Recherche modifiée — appuyez sur Entrée pour lancer la recherche.` while no visible Entrée control remained available because the iOS keyboard could already be dismissed. v141 therefore remains immutable and is not promotable.

The release line is now:

## 2. v141 physical finding and root cause

### 2.1 What worked physically

The v141 Search scrolling repair achieved its principal goal on physical iPhone: the Search results were naturally scrollable and readable. The v141 one-scroll-owner architecture and adaptive first-result reveal therefore remain protected achievements and are inherited by v142.

### 2.2 New release-blocking defect

Manual text entry exposed an independent submission problem. The Search input had:

- `type="search"`;
- an `oninput` path which cleared old results and displayed the pending instruction;
- a custom `keydown` handler which executed Search only when `event.key === 'Enter'`;
- no visible in-app submit action.

On iOS, the software keyboard is not guaranteed to remain visible after editing. The app could therefore instruct the user to activate a control which no longer existed on screen.

### 2.3 Deeper root cause

The defect was not merely “missing button”. The Search UI lacked an explicit distinction between:

- a **draft/pending query** currently being edited; and
- a **committed query** which had actually been submitted and whose results/filters were authoritative.

Different routes had inconsistent commit semantics: manual typing relied on keyboard Enter, while suggestion/recent-search/deep-link/restore paths and several filter changes could execute or rerun Search programmatically. The live status region was also being used to narrate every pending edit rather than only meaningful submitted/running/completed/error state changes.

## 3. v142 bounded repair

v142 is built directly from the exact frozen v141 tree `73cebf29a52e8051bb49b59eb8ec2d7ef5a10386` and package SHA-256 `c8951a8e3de087a72ebbd131bf42c54dfdbd5ceae91c5518ece798e8d2803836`.

The repair is deliberately narrow:

1. add a stable, always-visible **Rechercher** button below the Search input, disabled only when the trimmed query is empty;
2. wrap only the Search input / Clear / Rechercher controls in a native form with `role="search"`;
3. add `enterkeyhint="search"` and remove the custom Search-input `keydown` Enter handler;
4. make Clear explicitly `type="button"` and keep all Search filters outside the form;
5. make dynamically generated Jesus/Tome filter buttons explicitly `type="button"`;
6. introduce explicit `searchQueryPending` and `searchCommittedQuery` state;
7. manual input mutation enters pending state and does **not** execute Search;
8. Source/Tome/Order/Jesus/Search-intent/result-lane/pager changes rerun only a committed query, never silently submit a pending edit;
9. a draft pending query hides the Search live-status region rather than announcing a keyboard-only instruction;
10. suggestions remain explicit commit routes; deep-link and Reader-return restoration remain committed routes;
11. Help now makes **Rechercher** the primary action and keyboard Search/Entrée an equivalent shortcut;
12. v141 `#search-scroll`, ordinary-content `#search-results`, and adaptive `revealSearchOutput()` geometry are preserved.

## 1. Current governing position

A physical post-release use finding reopened the LDC Search presentation surface after v139 had been validly tested and deployed. The defect does **not** alter the fact that the production repository contains the exact tested v139 bytes. It does mean that v139 is now classified as **production / defect-known** for the Search-results usability issue described below.

→ **owner physical Search usability finding**

## 2. Owner physical finding and severity

The owner supplied physical iPhone and iPad screenshots and reported that Search results were generated but could not be meaningfully read or scrolled because the result region was squeezed into a very small strip at the bottom of the screen.

Observed evidence included:

- iPhone query `Professeur` with `Phrase exacte · 20` while the actual result content was almost entirely below the usable region;
- iPad query `Amour` with `Phrase exacte · 6772 · 308 entrées correspondantes` while the actual result content was similarly starved of vertical space;
- inability in practical use to scroll through and consume the results.

Classification:

- `SEVERITY = P0 functional usability / release-blocking for a successor`;
- `DATA_INTEGRITY_INCIDENT = NO`;
- `SEARCH_RESULT_GENERATION_FAILURE = NO`;
- `CORPUS_OR_RANKING_DEFECT = NOT INDICATED BY THIS FINDING`.

The Search engine was demonstrably producing result counts. The failure was in the presentation/scroll architecture that made those results inaccessible to a human user.

## 3. Root-cause determination

### 3.1 Primary architectural root cause

The v139 Search screen placed multiple non-shrinking control rows above `#search-results`, while `#search-results` was the only intended vertical Search result scroller and inherited `flex:1; min-height:0; overflow-y:auto`.

That made the result pane the sacrificial flex item. As available viewport height fell, Flexbox could shrink the human-visible results viewport toward zero while leaving the controls intact. Because the application body itself is scroll-locked, the result content remained trapped inside the collapsed nested scroller rather than naturally enlarging a single document scroll surface.

Controlled geometry reproduced the physical symptom, including realistic short landscape cases in which the result viewport reached `0 px`.

### 3.2 Secondary deterministic state defect

`onSearchInput()` hid `Parcourir par date` for a non-empty typed query, but `searchFor(term)` — used by frequent-theme and recent-search routes — set the query and ran Search without synchronizing that query-dependent chrome.

Therefore identical logical query state could produce different UI depending on entry route. In particular, the built-in `Amour` suggestion uses `searchFor('amour')`, explaining why `Parcourir par date` could remain visible in the physical screenshot and consume additional height.

### 3.3 QA-methodology lesson

Prior checks of Search correctness, width responsiveness, result DOM presence and horizontal overflow did not prove that a human had a usable vertical result viewport. Future Search qualification therefore requires **width × height** geometry and human-reachability invariants, not width-only responsive checks.

## 4. v140/R13 — frozen structural repair and supersession

v140/R13 was built as the first bounded successor from exact production v139.

### 4.2 v140 structural repair

v140 introduced the intended architecture:

1. one `#search-scroll` vertical Search-body scroller below the existing Search top bar;
2. all Search controls, metadata, warnings and results inside that one scroll surface;
3. `#search-results` converted to normal document content rather than a nested vertical scroller;
4. centralized query-state synchronization for clear-button/date-navigation visibility;
5. fresh-result output reveal without moving keyboard/accessibility focus;
6. Reader-return `preserve-context` policy using stable `.result-card[data-result-key]` restoration;
7. Search text-size reflow preservation bound to the same stable result-card semantics.

### 4.3 Why v140 did not progress to physical testing

A stricter post-freeze blind layout challenge tested **9 viewport geometries × 4 text levels = 36 cases**, including ultra-short viewport, Large/Très grand text, warning and suggestion chrome.

The structural single-scroll repair itself passed, and result reachability was restored, but the additional desired invariant — **the first complete result should be fully visible immediately after fresh-result reveal** — failed in 3/36 extreme cases:

- `320 × 480`, Large: first-result bottom ≈ 17 px below viewport;
- `320 × 480`, Très grand: ≈ 52 px below viewport;
- `375 × 500`, Très grand: ≈ 14 px below viewport.

Because v140 already had an exact frozen identity and App-Test candidate, APP-GOV prohibited silently rewriting it. It was therefore frozen and superseded before any owner physical test.

`v140/R13 = HISTORICAL FROZEN FAILED CANDIDATE / DO NOT TEST / DO NOT PROMOTE`.

## 5. v141/R14 — current bounded successor

v141 is a direct immutable successor of v140. It preserves the v140 structural repair and adds only an adaptive fresh-result reveal hardening.

### 5.1 Adaptive reveal behavior

After the preferred result metadata is positioned near the top of `#search-scroll`, v141 measures the first `.result-card` against the actual Search viewport.

If the first card already fits, no additional movement occurs.

If its bottom extends below the Search viewport, v141 advances `scrollTop` only by the exact remaining overflow, capped to the maximum valid scroll position. This preserves as much result context as possible while making the first complete result visible when geometrically possible.

The operation:

- changes scroll position only;
- does **not** move DOM/keyboard/VoiceOver focus;
- is not executed for Reader-return restoration;
- leaves stable result-key restoration authoritative for Reader return and text-size changes.

### 5.2 Mutation boundary

- `offline_manifest.json`;
- `sw.js`;
- `version.json`.

All **205 `corpus/` files are byte-identical** to v139.

Protected Search modules are byte-identical to v139, including:

## 9. Required owner physical test for v141

The physical test should be intentionally small but cover the defect and regression risks.

### iPhone and iPad — required core checks

1. Open the v141 App-Test route.
2. Search **Amour** using the built-in/recent-search route if available.
3. Confirm the Search automatically presents a **fully readable first result**, rather than leaving results squeezed at the bottom.
4. Scroll through several results; confirm the entire Search body behaves as one natural vertical scroll surface.
5. Scroll upward; confirm the Search field and filters remain reachable.
6. Confirm `Parcourir par date` is **not** displayed while a non-empty query is active.
7. Change at least one of Source / Ordre / Jesus filter / Tome group / result lane and confirm the refreshed result set remains readable.
8. Open a result, then **Retour**; confirm the same result position is restored rather than jumping to result 1/top.
9. Change text size while on Search (preferably to **Très grand**) and confirm the visible result remains sensibly anchored and results remain scrollable/readable.
10. Clear the query; confirm the date navigator/suggestions return normally.

### iPad landscape emphasis

Repeat a Search in landscape because short available height was a primary failure mode in v139.

### Pass criterion

The gate closes only if the owner reports the exact v141 App-Test candidate behaves correctly on the relevant iPhone/iPad tests. A failure creates a new successor; v141 itself is not edited.

- an external dependency or browser/PWA behaviour invalidates a release-critical assumption;
- documentary evidence materially contradicts the current State;
- the owner explicitly reopens a governed decision.

A reopened issue does not authorize mutation automatically. Root cause, exact scope, mutation authority, protected surfaces, successor identity and requalification requirements must first be established.

## 4. Root causes and bounded corrections

### 4.1 v136 release-integrity defect

**Defect.** The v136 page identity had advanced, but material current release bindings had not all advanced with it. `sw.js` still named v135/R8 shell/runtime caches and `version.json` retained stale v135 current-state metadata.

**Root cause.** Incomplete successor release-binding propagation across the page → worker → cache → metadata chain.

**Correction.** v137 rebound page/worker/cache/current metadata consistently. Protected corpus/Search/provenance/user-state content was not changed for this correction.

### 4.2 Dark secondary-button contrast defect

Fresh full-QA review found the dark `.btn-secondary` foreground `#8A7E72` on `#2A2418` below the project 4.5:1 normal-text target. The bounded v138 correction raised the foreground to `#A89B8E` without changing structure or control semantics.

Final measured blind-challenge contrast for the repaired secondary surface: **5.6775:1**. The `Reprendre` control remained high contrast at approximately **7.87:1** in current-runtime evidence.

### 4.3 Inherited Search-V2.1A authority defect

**v137 layer.** `search_worker_v2.js` still carried predecessor Search manifest authority hashes, so the fail-closed worker could not validly bind to the packaged current manifests.

**v138 layer.** Rebinding those hashes correctly exposed a deeper invariant failure: `SEARCH-V2.1A aflp token-count mismatch`.

**Root cause.** The Stage-2 topology reference block had not been re-certified after the corpus generation advanced. Its stored token counts represented the older `>=3`-character BM25-style count basis, while exact Search-V2.1A intentionally reconstructs **all non-empty visible tokens**. The package itself labelled the Stage-2 reference as not re-certified. The failure was therefore stale certification metadata, not a need to weaken the fail-closed guard and not a defect requiring mutation of the devotional corpus or matching/ranking algorithms.

**v139 correction.** Re-certify the existing current logical-unit topology against the current all-nonempty-visible-token contract and regenerate only the dependent integrity/binding metadata.

Re-certified authority:

| Mode | Units | Tokens | Deterministic digest |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| AFLP | 2,312 | 1,466,870 | `6bc37d012a23154af2d669cddb3f84078de606fadb43da3ab1dba516639a6c0f` |
| Additions | 75 | 14,333 | `029c8f53c9a20cae460ff2ef8e76c82cbc50bba4aa518b357eabe1019f4c2c16` |
| Enriched | 2,325 | 1,480,956 | `49bc61ea97e2218da594a713748da0f21beefabef4762516cdb14b4af42b1544` |

The exhaustive Search qualification exercised **4,712 logical units** and **129 deeper exact-in-unit probes**. Representative current queries `bateau`, `de`, `je`, `volonté`, NFD `volonté`, `divine volonté`, and a bounded near-search perturbation all passed.

### 4.4 Apparent offline persistence failure — harness defect, not app defect

The first v139 current-runtime run observed UI state `READY` / `204 of 204` but sampled the persisted IndexedDB record as `NOT_PREPARED`. Because the app deliberately debounces persistence by 200 ms, the original asynchronous harness assertion sampled too early.

A dedicated diagnostic run tested both:

- offline preparation without backup/restore; and
- backup/restore followed by offline preparation.

In both scenarios the record progressed deterministically to persisted `READY` after the debounce and remained stable. Diagnostic evidence commit: `923b8ccb7a8ebe6f15a60b32cd810d5a5787f749`.

**Correction:** harness timing only. **No v139 application byte changed.** The current-runtime harness was changed to poll committed IndexedDB state from the test driver, then the entire five-gate workflow was rerun. Final current-runtime result: PASS.

## 1. v127 user-visible contracts

### 1.1 One global text-size setting

There remains exactly one persistent text-size preference: `Petit / Normal / Grand / Très grand`.

There is **no** Help-specific or per-screen size preference and no automatic screen-based switching. Direct access is exposed on the principal substantive non-Reader screens; Reader retains `⋯ → Taille du texte`. The user may deliberately choose Très grand while in Help and later choose Grand while reading a normal text; each action changes the same persisted preference.

The text-size change captures/restores the active screen's semantic/visual scroll context so reflow does not unnecessarily displace the reader. Reader retains its semantic position mechanism.

### 1.2 Mon Espace tabs

The six workspace sections now use tab semantics with `aria-selected`, roving tabindex, tabpanel relationships and Arrow/Home/End keyboard movement. Visual state and programmatic state must remain synchronized.

### 1.3 Authored editable-control names

Authored accessible names cover the personal note editor, new collection name, collection-item note and optional text-issue comment. Placeholder-only identification is not accepted for these surfaces.

### 1.4 Shared modal focus

Shared modal open/close ordering captures the invoker before background inert and restores invoker focus after inert is removed. This contract applies to the size chooser and other dialogs using the same helper.

- Reader and `Infos et source` are reactivated/repositioned in the same task, followed by later verification.

## 1. R3 defect analysis and implemented transaction contract

### 1.1 Root cause

R2 used a one-shot scroll model around `display:none → display:flex` overflow containers. It restored a numeric `scrollTop` once, moved focus in a neighbouring frame, and never verified that the browser retained the requested value after layout/focus reconciliation.

The physical result proved that model insufficient on the target WebKit/PWA environment.

### 1.2 Repair

The provenance transition is now a bounded transaction:

`capture raw position + CTA visual offset → activate destination → establish focus → restore → verify in later animation frames → one bounded late correction → cleanup`.

Key protections:

- provenance always reopens at absolute top;
- Help return captures both `scrollTop` and the Help provenance CTA's viewport-relative position;
- Reader-info return preserves Reader scroll, sheet scroll, and reader-info CTA viewport-relative position;
- restoration occurs after focus rather than trusting `preventScroll` alone;
- one 80 ms late verification protects against delayed scroll reconciliation;
- trusted pointer/touch/wheel/keyboard interaction immediately cancels the late correction so the app cannot snap an actively scrolling user back;
- `overflow-anchor:none` is temporary and local to the affected scroller only;
- superseded transitions are explicitly cancelled and cleaned up.

No global scrolling CSS or browser-history behaviour was changed.

The title remains **Infos et source**.

The ordinary layer now prioritizes source/page/reference/date information and the contextual methodology CTA. Raw internal processing status, raw source code, corpus IDs, locator/authority fields and Tome governance state move under collapsed **Détails techniques**.

There is no universal public PRINCIPAL `Vérifié`, `Revue effectuée` or equivalent status in v126.

The five known PRINCIPAL raw source-edition values are governed by an explicit fail-closed presentation table. Ambiguous raw `2021` (2,165 entries) and `GELDC17-2024` (2 entries) do not receive guessed friendly edition names. Unknown future values also fail closed.

### 3.4 Full methodology

The public methodology screen has:

The former project-facing label `Révision finale R12` is absent from the public layer. Substantive documentary evidence is preserved and reorganized rather than silently discarded.

---

## 4. Diagnostic/privacy architecture

The raw navigation trace may still observe literal keyboard `key` values during its short qualification window. v126 therefore does **not** attach the raw trace to the ordinary diagnostic.

A dedicated public sanitizer:

- categorizes navigation/activation/escape-tab keys;
- replaces one-character printable keys with `printable-key-redacted`;
- bounds the exported trace;
- leaves normal `Copier le diagnostic` functional if trace serialization/collection fails.

The public Help copy states the diagnostic may include recent navigation/display state and public passage identifiers but excludes literal typed characters, search terms, annotations, selected text and paragraph content.

---

## 5. Origin-aware return contract

Help → methodology → Help preserves Help scroll/focus context.

Reader `Infos et source` → methodology → Reader captures Reader scroll, entry/Tome/supplement identity, source mode and sheet scroll. On return it restores the same context if identity remains valid; otherwise it fails safely to the Reader without fabricating stale state.

This is presentation/navigation-shell routing only and does not introduce persistent state.

## 3. Why v125 exists

The v124 Help screen technically responded to the application's four text-size levels, but its scaling curve was too restrained for the nature of the content. A fresh DOM recount during the independent v125 recheck finds about **2,800 words across the Help screen** (tokenization-dependent), including **2,415 words in `.help-text` body elements**, together with **74 explanatory rows**, **11 major sections** and **6 callouts/tips**. It therefore functions as a substantive secondary reading surface rather than merely compact interface chrome.

At v124 the Help body curve was:

`13 / 14 / 16 / 18 px`

while the Reader grew much more strongly. This produced the user-visible impression that Help barely changed, particularly at `Grand` and `Très grand`.

The bounded v125 change strengthens Help/documentation typography while preserving Reader typography and all semantic/application data.

---

## 5. Architectural implementation decision

The change is intentionally isolated.

- Existing dedicated `--help-body-size` remains the Help/documentation body variable.
- Existing dedicated `--help-tip-size` remains the Help callout variable.
- A new dedicated `--help-title-size` variable controls Help section titles.
- `.help-section-title` was removed from the unrelated shared `--sem-strong-15` selector so Help-title growth cannot unintentionally enlarge other interface elements.
- A normal-size root default `--help-title-size:16px` was added so Help headings have a defined value before stored preferences finish loading.
- Help chips retain the existing semantic compact scale.
- Provenance/source explanatory body text intentionally continues to share `--help-body-size`, because it is also documentation/reading content.

This establishes the practical hierarchy:

`Reader content → Help/provenance documentation → excerpts → interface → metadata`.

# R35 ADDENDUM — FROZEN SOURCE-LEVEL FORENSICS AND RELEASE-DECISION ANALYSIS

# Livre du Ciel v142.19 — R35 root-cause and release-decision review

**Date:** 8 October 2026. **Authority:** Read-only technical and documentary analysis; no application mutation, deployment, browser-data manipulation, or new release authorisation. **Baseline:** v142.19 beta GitHub `bce95d482b9b7dad6ae01638c16154e824bcfa78`, production GitHub `99711c554b5c63c6fdbc16f2e7d11980e2567d1b`, App-Test GitHub `572d9df7927765b575a76eaee98fd3cc9d455e74`. **Governing predecessor:** R34 cumulative State. **Primary external inputs:** both owner-supplied ClaudeCode v142.18/v142.19 HTML audits; actual current GitHub source and calibration evidence; owner physical v142.19 PASS for the two reported Reader faults.

## Executive decision

**Preserve v142.19's physically accepted Reader. Treat semantic search as a separate multi-layer relevance and presentation problem, not simply a high threshold. Protect personal data before further testing.** The next step should be a small, *read-only* query-trace and policy-comparison exercise. Do not adjust thresholds, rebuild indexes, alter the Reader, clear caches, rewrite GitHub, or deploy on the basis of this analysis. The current production GitHub tree has v142.19 files, but independently confirming Pages delivery and installed-service-worker activation is outstanding.

### Material R35 findings beyond R34

1. **F-01C, source-demonstrated: hidden hard constraints from approximate memories.** The actual `searchSemanticV3ParseStructural()` turns `vers 1919`, `tome 12 ou 13`, or `1900 ou 1901` into strict year/volume constraints, removing the first captured token from the semantic query; the UI does not visibly expose an editable interpretation. The correct passage can be excluded *before* semantic retrieval. The previously proposed confidence correction cannot address that class of false negative.
2. **F-01D, source-demonstrated: entry-level evaluation can overestimate passage-level correctness.** Fusion deduplicates to an `entry_id`; when dense and BM25 favour different spans within the same entry, the output excerpt and target passage come from the first dense-row representative. An audit reporting a 'correct entry in top 20' has not necessarily shown that the right paragraph is available, highlighted, or navigable. Verified with the real `fuse()` function and synthetic candidate rows.
3. **F-01E, source-demonstrated: calibration assertions are narrow and the threshold is hard-pinned.** `HYBRID_DENSE_ABSTENTION_V1` threshold `0.8845798510542678` is hard-coded in the pack guard *as well as* in the manifest and associated evidence; the runtime pins the manifest SHA-256. A 'one-line threshold change' would fail qualification unless guard, evidence, runtime binding, hashes, release artifacts and governance are reconciled. Silently bypassing the gate in UI would also change the product's evidence claims. One previously revealed V1-negative/truth-neutral probe with dense score `0.8912556818026742` already receives `possible`, showing that the limited PASS gates are not a general rejection guarantee.
4. **F-01F, source-demonstrated: the confidence score is not a posterior probability and is attached only to the first fused entry.** `0.88458` is an E5 cosine-like dense-similarity discriminator with overlapping observed positives and negatives, not an 88.46% probability of relevance. Its choice from three owner-positive examples does not establish calibrated user-facing certainty.
5. **E-02, source-confirmed contract gap: cold-offline semantic search is not guaranteed.** The semantic manifest uses `fetch(...,{cache:'no-store'})` and is excluded from the service worker's application-shell list; in a new offline execution context it cannot be relied on to initialise. Warm-session success is not an offline reliability qualification. This matters more if the app claims all of *Par le sens* is offline.
6. **Release integrity is separate from model qualification.** The shipped semantic pack identifies `deployment_authorized:false` and `app_runtime_wired:false`, while it is imported by a page whose production GitHub tree now includes this runtime. Those fields are part of a frozen engineering evidence tuple and the loader explicitly *requires* them to be false; they cannot safely be flipped as a release fix. Instead release attestation must be tracked externally and separately. Do not infer from the discrepancy alone that the owner's deployment was unauthorised.
7. **A systemic storage-pressure interaction is plausible.** Beta/production share an origin for ordinary Safari IndexedDB; old workers may preserve additional 114.5 MB-class corpus cache copies; semantic assets are large and HTTP/CacheStorage retention is nontrivial. Offline corpus assets are scope-keyed while IndexedDB is origin-keyed. The total space and eviction implications on real iPhones remain unmeasured; avoid destructive cache experiments and export valuable annotations first.

### Statistical caution: the reported 12-query change is material but not representative

ClaudeCode states that the same twelve descriptions yielded 11 displayed known target entries in v142.14 and only 3 in v142.19. If these are truly the **same binary, paired twelve items**, their unknown overlap must be either two or three. The exact paired McNemar test would then give two-sided p values approximately **0.0215** or **0.0078**, respectively. This reinforces that the within-fixture collapse is not a trivial numerical fluctuation. **It does not prove population-wide performance**: the set is small, curated, and 'correct entry' is a less demanding endpoint than correct paragraph or a human judgement of best match. By contrast the top-1 shift 9→5 on twelve examples is not decisive and needs independent relevance adjudication.

## Search failure taxonomy — do not mix causes

The user sees the same unsuccessful-search outcome for several distinct mechanisms:

- **A. Scope exclusion:** `searchSemanticV3ParseStructural` silently turns remembered date/Tome clues into hard constraints, potentially excluding the true entry. Confidence changes cannot repair it.
- **B. Retrieval miss:** neither dense 160-candidate window nor BM25 160-candidate window retrieves the relevant passage; new index/ranking work may be necessary.
- **C. Entry collapse / wrong paragraph:** a relevant entry is found, but the returned representative text is the first dense span, not necessarily the intended phrase. An entry-level hit may be a false UX success.
- **D. Fusion rank shift:** true candidate is retrieved but placed lower when unequal passages or entry-level RRF are combined. Compare dense rank, BM25 rank and fused rank explicitly.
- **E. Global confidence abstention:** the first fused candidate fails threshold/two-channel requirement and all 20 results are discarded regardless of their own evidence.
- **F. Presentation/interaction failure:** relevant excerpt shown but cannot navigate precisely to the desired paragraph/span, cannot maintain scroll, or sends the user to unrelated text.
- **G. Initialization unavailable:** model/manifest/cache/memory/network failure; cannot legitimately be labelled a relevance failure.

This decomposition changes the repair order and the acceptance ledger. A threshold-only approach addresses E partly, not A–D or F–G.

## Source-level experimental evidence added in R35

### Hidden constraint examples (real unmodified parser executed in memory)

| Input typed into Par le sens | Parsed by current code | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| `vers 1919 Jésus parle du soleil de la volonté divine` | `year=1919`; residual `vers Jésus parle du soleil de la volonté divine` | Approximate year becomes exact; otherwise relevant 1918/1920 entries are impossible to retrieve. |
| `dans le tome 12 ou le tome 13, je crois` | `volume=12`; residual retains `le tome 13, je crois` | Only Tome 12 is searched despite explicit uncertainty and alternate Tome 13. |
| `en 1900 ou 1901 Jésus parle de l'humilité` | `year=1900`; residual still mentions 1901 | Tome/chronology evidence may be incorrect without any warning. |
| `une parole autour du 1er mai 1900` | `dateIso=1900-05-01`; residual `une parole autour du` | Hedged date is treated as an exact day. |
| `1900` | `structuralOnly=true` | Delegated to lexical structural search rather than semantic engine; valid but the switch needs honest UI messaging. |

**Design implication:** treat dates, Tome numbers and references as *explicit constraints* only when the user unambiguously selects them or when the interface reveals the interpreted criteria with a one-tap way to remove them. 'Vers', 'environ', 'peut-être', 'ou' and uncertain clues should preferably be soft ranking hints or untreated natural language, not silent exclusions. Do not implement a naive regex for uncertainty as a patch: the grammar requires representative adversarial examples and source-preserving fallbacks.

### Entry-versus-span ambiguity (real unmodified `fuse()` executed in memory)

For entry `E1`, the dense channel returned passage `E1-partA` (a different paragraph) while BM25 returned `E1-partB` (the actually desired text). Current `fuse()` combined their ranks to put entry `E1` first, but returned `E1-partA` as its `passage_id`/excerpt. The UI converts **that selected passage's** first `source_span` into the navigation target. Hence 'correct entry ranked first' does not ensure that the intended quoted words appear, are highlighted, or are reached after opening. This should be independently checked on the twelve natural descriptions, especially for long entries (e.g. 30 May 1932 with 210 paragraphs).

**Metric upgrade:** for each known answer record **canonical target paragraph/span**, not only `entry_id`. Report entry@1/5/20 and paragraph@1/5/20; then measure tap-to-correct-span on actual rendered results. Permit multiple relevant passages per description where the text itself supports them. A single 'target entry' can misclassify a genuinely relevant alternative as wrong.

### Calibration evidence and hard-code constraints

The three owner-positive top dense scores are about 0.89990, 0.90727 and 0.90746. The eight development negatives have a maximum about 0.86926. Their midpoint is exactly the deployed **0.8845798510542678**. The four new V2 holdout negatives are between about 0.85008 and 0.87570. A previously revealed V1 probe designated among 'revealed truth-neutral probes' scores about **0.89126** and is classified **`possible`**, despite not having a known intended entry. This is not proof that the guard violates its formal truth-neutrality protocol, but disproves any *simplistic* claim that the policy refuses every previously seen negative-like query.

The classifier additionally conflates `null` dense scores with numeric zero in some diagnostic fields because `Number(null)===0`. Under the current threshold this is not a demonstrated extra result-visibility bug; it does make the feature data harder to interpret reliably when calibrating future policies.

**Release dependency:** `search_semantic_pack_guard_r4.js` hard-requires the exact threshold and `possible_min_channels=2`. `pls_v16/semantic_pack_manifest.json` repeats the policy; its calibration evidence must contain the *identical* policy, and `pls_v16/runtime_v1.mjs` requires the manifest's SHA-256 to match an embedded constant. Changing any of these also affects package/offline integrity and release identity. Therefore do not patch the threshold or loosen the registry's behaviour while continuing to present the old pack as calibrated and qualified. A new labelled policy and correctly rebuilt evidence are essential.

## Proposed user experience: prioritise retrieval while truthfully communicating uncertainty

**Product objective:** recover a remembered Livre du Ciel passage without asserting that a machine match is the intended passage, exact quote, or doctrinally verified claim. False negative = hide a retrievable passage; false positive = show a clearly labelled suggestion that the user can assess. A simple threshold cannot optimize both with overlapping observed score distributions.

**Compare three alternatives on exactly the same frozen candidates before choosing:**

- **A. Current rejection (`control`)**: highest apparent caution but demonstrably hides relevant candidate lists; leave only as regression baseline.
- **B. Always show 20**: maximizes recoverability; risks clutter and misleading weak queries. Requires cautious language everywhere.
- **C. Recommended first prototype — transparent optional exploration:** show normal ranked results when there is plausible evidence; otherwise state `Aucune correspondance convaincante n'a été identifiée` and offer **`Voir les passages les plus proches (à vérifier)`**. This disclosure is explicit, reader-initiated, non-authoritative; do **not** say there are no passages when the ranking engine has 20. The visible state must explain that suggestions can be unrelated. The button must remain easy to find and work with VoiceOver. Avoid fabricated percentages/confidence badges or doctrine checks.

This is an **experimental design choice**, not pre-approved code. It must be evaluated on real remembered descriptions and unrelated inputs. The policy for outright empty results should distinguish actual zero eligible candidates from nonzero weakly ranked candidates. No silent fallback to `Par les mots` while claiming `Par le sens`.

### Evaluation sample and rules

1. Freeze the precise corpus, source mode, filters, semantic pack, model revision and query text before comparison. Require raw per-query output and script (the ClaudeCode HTML reports did not supply these). Rerun all 12 natural descriptions, the 3 owner queries, the 216 title variants and nine previously unreachable entries; supplement with about 15–25 fresh natural descriptions written without seeing candidate results. Also include fresh unrelated/near-domain descriptions.
2. Log: parsed filters, dense 160 passage candidates, BM25 160 passage candidates, entry-collapse mapping, fused 20 entries, selected span, confidence features, display treatment and clicked target. Do **not** record personal notes, highlights or user identifiers. Reproducibility and protection of local data take precedence.
3. Blindly adjudicate at least the first five results for the natural-description sample, with 'clearly relevant / plausible related / unrelated' and canonical target span; preserve multiple correct passages where the text justifies it.
4. Compare **entry recall@20**, **correct span recall@20**, **precision/relevance@5**, median reciprocal rank, *percent of queries with useful displayed target*, empty-result rate, out-of-domain misleading presentation, and latency/memory change. Track hard-filter false exclusions separately.
5. No unqualified 'PASS' from the three calibrated positives alone. A policy that improves displayed recall but materially degrades reader trust or points to the wrong paragraph is not accepted. A direct-code unit PASS and a physical iPhone PASS are separate gates.
6. Exact deployment candidate must use a new immutable version, have independent build/package checks, and be tested without modifying production personal storage. Commit or production promotion requires separate explicit authorisation.

## Parallel operational findings and dependencies

### Storage separation is prerequisite for risky testing

On ordinary Safari the two repository paths are the **same web origin**, with the **same IndexedDB database `ldc_user_v1`**; restoring or deleting records in one path can affect the other. By contrast the worker's offline caches use a scope fingerprint, so cache data can be distinct even while notes are shared. On standalone iOS PWAs, storage segregation may differ and must be established using **throwaway records**. A distinct hostname (not merely a new repository under `louisriv26.github.io`) is the preferred test environment. Never tell the owner to clear Safari website data or remove installed icons to validate a fix. Back up first before any authorised migration.

### Memory and offline requirements are product decisions, not just code bugs

The semantic runtime hashes large model segments and reloads them; repeated fetch operations do not necessarily imply duplicate internet bytes. Its first use is substantial (~100 MB network, Chrome peak memory ~1.2–1.4 GB per auditor), and iOS performance has not been measured. Cold-offline restart is not guaranteed because the manifest uses `no-store` and is not in the service-worker shell. Explicitly choose whether **offline reading only** or **offline *Par le sens* after preparation** is in scope. The latter implies storage, versioned model caches, integrity-on-reuse, and potentially eviction trade-offs. Avoid rearchitecting the loader until one low-memory physical Apple device is measured.

### Search fidelity qualification must trace back to canonical Reader text

The 74,528/74,528 coverage ratio only proves every **declared topology record** reaches the semantic index. It cannot detect a paragraph tail absent from the topology itself. The audit's seven tails (~240 words) should be reproduced by a per-paragraph start-to-end coverage comparator that accounts for supplements, normalized offsets, overlap and gaps. Source changes must not be invented to make the index pass. Exact phrase, semantic and screenshot jump checks should be repeated for each repaired span; derived index, embeddings and hashes may need coherent rebuild. Report the exact seven source IDs and missing UTF-16/canonical ranges, not just total words.

### Release attestations are not the same as model calibration

The shipped manifest still says `deployment_authorized:false` and `app_runtime_wired:false`; the runtime checks this frozen engineering contract. Since production GitHub includes the runtime, release authorisation must reside in a separately governed release attestation (owner approval, CI, candidate/package hash, device gates, deployment provenance), not be inferred or retrofitted by flipping immutable pack metadata. This distinction should be made explicit in the cumulative governing State.

## Revised work priority and gating

| Workstream | Impact / probability | Relative effort and dependency | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Preserve Reader v142.19 | Proven physical success on two critical flows | No source changes | **FREEZE** |
| Protect test/production personal data | Potential irreversible loss in shared browser store | Separate origin + backups; no destructive tests before isolation | **P0 TEST SAFETY** |
| F-01 candidate/presentation trace | High current impact, high confidence in global rejection | Read-only script and known-item fixtures; no model rebuild | **NEXT — P1** |
| F-01 hidden approximate dates/Tomes | Mechanism proven, real incidence unknown | Parser/UI adjustments require authorisation and UX tests | **P1 diagnostic, bounded successor only if material** |
| F-01 entry-to-paragraph jump | Mechanism proven, incidence unknown | Needs span-level answer labels, representative logic challenge | **P1 diagnostic** |
| Semantic soft-result interaction | Can recover hidden candidates without false certainty | Changes registry + UI + calibration attestation; new candidate | **P1 candidate after tests** |
| F-06 source-span fidelity | Small reported missing area, important exact-text credibility | Rebuild dependency must be mapped | **P1 separate integrity repair** |
| Cold-offline semantic contract | Expected behaviour undecided; current technical limitation | Potentially large storage/runtime scope | **Decision first** |
| F-04 cache corruption retry | Recoverability risk, low demonstrated frequency | Bounded retry; protect data | **P1 later** |
| F-05 mobile loading/memory | High cost possible on older iPhones, unmeasured there | Profile before engineering | **P1 later** |
| F-02 large-iPhone compact UI | No user-reported failure after v142.19 PASS | CSS regression risk disproportionate | **DEFER** |
| F-08 intentional `/ldc/` removal | Historical shortcut compatibility | Owner policy needed; no automatic resurrection/cleanup | **OPTIONAL** |

## Precise next step and stop conditions

**Next authorised action to consider: READ-ONLY F-01 forensic harness, not a patch.** Its deliverables: frozen query set, reproducible end-to-end trace, per-query diagnosis (scope/retrieval/entry-fusion/global suppression/UI), representative wrong-span examples, three policy alternatives on the *same* candidates, and a decision memo. Do not promote a successor until source-to-package integrity, synthetic/browser checks, and owner physical iPhone/iPad verification are satisfied for the changed surfaces. If a failure cannot be reproduced from frozen evidence, do not describe it as independently PASS/FAIL.

**Stop/go:** no code mutation on R35; stop destructive storage experiments under shared origin; do not silently change hard-pinned pack qualifications; do not reopen the Reader. The final choice between an opt-in exploration button and direct cautious result display depends on fresh query evidence and the owner's preference for reader simplicity.

**Current production publication limitation:** production GitHub main contains v142.19 files and matches Beta, but a new independent HTTP GitHub Pages / installed-iOS version check was *not obtained*. A web-fetch attempt returned unavailable and must not be treated as proof of a live deployment failure. No rollback recommended without evidence of a production regression.
